title: Local setup-* wrapper actions must call the upstream actions/setup-* directly
answers: Why does the review flag actions/setup-python inside .github/actions/setup-python as recursive?
Can a composite action wrapper call actions/setup-node itself?
Should I replace upstream actions/setup-* calls inside the local setup wrappers?
body:
The local wrappers under .github/actions/setup-python, setup-node and setup-java are the implementation of the wrapper, so their steps must call the upstream actions/setup-* actions.
The upstream call is at .github/actions/setup-python/action.yml:runs.steps (line ~60), .github/actions/setup-node/action.yml:runs.steps (line ~12) and .github/actions/setup-java/action.yml:runs.steps (line ~17).
Do not rewrite these calls to the local wrapper; that makes the action call itself.
The workflow guidance in .claude/rules/github-actions.md says to replace direct actions/setup-* usage with the wrappers. That advice is for consumers, and nothing mechanical (dev/check_actions.py, .github/policy.rego) enforces it, so the wrappers are not exempted in the file.
applies: Edits to the setup-python, setup-node or setup-java composite actions, or reviews of any composite action that wraps an upstream action.
says: Code review flags the shared setup action as calling itself in an infinite loop.
Reviewers ask why the custom setup wrapper calls the official upstream action directly.
A pull request comment suggests replacing upstream setup steps inside the wrapper definition.
The environment setup action fails by recursively invoking itself during continuous integration runs.
search: Composite action wrappers under `.github/actions/setup-python`, `setup-node`, and `setup-java` must call the upstream `actions/setup-*` actions directly within their step definitions. Replacing these upstream calls with the local wrapper causes recursive self-invocation. General rules advising repository workflows to use local wrappers apply only to consumers and are not mechanically enforced or exempted by `dev/check_actions.py` or `.github/policy.rego`.
